title: Effectiveness of playing the instruments „Big Bom“ and “Temple Blocks” as a music therapy approach to improve gait function among patients with multiple sclerosis.
summary: The objective of this study is to evaluate the effectiveness of music therapy on gait function among patients with multiple sclerosis, by playing the instruments „Big Bom“ and „Temple Blocks“. Patients will undergo 8 sessions of individual music therapy intervention in a neurological rehabilitation setting.

interventions.name: A physiotherapist will inform the patients regarding the content, and course of the study and will also give information about inclusion and exclusion criteria. The first assessment will be the Performance Oriented Mobility Assessment (POMA) which will determine the adherence to the study. Thereafte
Patients of group B, receive each three times, six- minutes of playing on the „Temple Blocks“. The music therapist will accompany on the piano. As mentioned, this is the control group.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients have to be diagnosed with Multiple sclerosis(McDonald 2018), Minimum age: 18 years old, ability to sit without support, legs apart, at least 30 minutes, no orthopedic limitation – especially joint limitation which can limit the range of arm motion, ability to transfer without support onto the „Big Bom“ , between 15 and 24 points in the Performance oriented mobility assessment (POMA). The Expanded disability status scale (EDSS) should be between 4.0 and 6.5 points. Signed consent form
Exclusion criteria:
Cortisone infusion/administration or exacerbation of the disease in the last/ of the past 30 days, new immunosuppressing medication, which may have side effects, during the last 3 months. Total hip arthroplasty (THA) in the last year. Attention deficits or cognitive limitation - a 30 minutes session is required. Acoustic deficits or visual impairments, which can interfere with the intervention. Hemiplegic or paraplegic patients. Limitation of shoulder range of motion, which can interfere with the Intervention. Urinary catheter, which may bother the sitting position. Patients who already take part in music or art therapy sessions (regarding for example mental stability)
